audit_findings.title: Rabbi-trust assets may be added without the matching deferred-compensation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.735 million bridge overstatement; $2.72 per share; 10.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds Rabbi-trust assets to equity without deducting the deferred-compensation claim those assets fund.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the total amount of our obligations under these plans was $57.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error. At June 30, 2026, filed Rabbi-trust assets were $61.881 million and deferred-compensation liabilities were $57.016 million ($8.810 million current plus $48.206 million long-term), leaving only a $4.865 million surplus. Using $56.6 million therefore overstates the bridge by $51.735 million. Correcting only this item would reduce base equity value from $477.0 million to $425.265 million and base value per share from $25.04 to about $22.32.
audit_findings.action: Replace the $56.6 million bridge item with a fully reconciled June 30, 2026 net surplus of no more than $4.865 million, confirm whether any trust assets are unavailable to common equity, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud-implementation cash costs may escape the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.mechanism: If owner earnings add back cloud-cost amortization but deduct only investing-section capital expenditures, operating-section cloud implementation payments are omitted from the reinvestment deduction, overstating the OE anchor and its projected cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Capitalized cloud computing costs are included in Other assets, net in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets and within operating activities on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting pathway is demonstrated, but an owner-earnings error is not yet demonstrated because the supplied record does not show the calculation ledger. The filed net cloud asset increased from $6.3 million to $20.0 million during 2025 and to $26.6 million by June 30, 2026, indicating substantial continuing investment, but those net balances do not establish the annual cash payments or the amount, if any, omitted from OE. Given a $29.9 million anchor, an omission could be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual cloud-implementation cash payments, capitalized balances and amortization to each OE calculation; deduct the cash outlays or cease adding back their amortization, then establish and rerun using a sustainable post-implementation maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain explicitly non-recurring restructuring costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.4 million pretax; approximately $2.311 million after tax, or 7.7% of the $29.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A genuinely non-recurring expense retained in 2025 net income reduces the OE anchor and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: In the fourth quarter of 2025, we recognized charges of $3.4 million related to refinements in our organizational structure and other non-recurring costs, which negatively impacted earnings per share for the fourth quarter of 2025 and fiscal 2025 by $0.13, net of the related tax effect.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE and appropriate normalization remain unresolved. The filed $0.13 diluted-EPS effect implies approximately $2.311 million after tax using 17.776 million diluted weighted-average shares. If fully retained and genuinely non-recurring, restoring it would raise the anchor by about 7.7% and increase base equity value by approximately $32.5 million, or $1.70 per current valuation share. Recurring realignment or software-write-off costs should not be normalized away.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.4 million charge through the 2025 OE build, separate the $1.2 million organizational-realignment component from the other $2.2 million, compare analogous charges across prior years and 2026, and rerun only the supportable non-recurring portion.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling may double-count issued restricted shares
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum tested denominator overstatement of 1.144 million shares; base value impact up to $1.59 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding issued RSAs or performance shares already included in legal common shares outstanding duplicates those claims in the fully diluted denominator and understates per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 Plan allows for the issuance of stock options, stock appreciation rights (“SARs”), stock awards (including restricted stock awards (“RSAs”) and restricted stock units (“RSUs”)) and other stock-based awards, such as Performance-Based Awards (collectively referred to as “Restricted Stock”).
audit_findings.explanation: The award-type split is unresolved, but the filed numbers permit a conservative upper-bound test. The 19.053 million denominator equals 17.909 million reported shares plus all 1.144 million outstanding restricted-stock awards. Even if every award were already included and the entire 1.144 million addition were removed, base value would rise only from $25.04 to about $26.63 and bull value from $27.61 to about $29.37, both still far below the $54.53 market price. The valuation conclusion therefore does not change under the maximum possible correction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the RSA, RSU, performance-award, option and SAR roll-forward; identify awards already included in reported shares; and replace the ceiling with an unduplicated treasury-stock-method dilution schedule.
